examples.text: 나 봐라, 예고도 없이 술 먹고 그냥 확 뱉었다가 준모랑 얼마나 어색해지고 이 고생이니! 방송에만 예고가 중요한 게 아니야, 현실에서도 중요해.
examples.trans: Look at me—I blurted mine out over drinks with zero preview, and look how awkward things got with Joon-mo! Previews matter in real life too, not just on television.

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 뱉다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (blurted out and then).

meanings.note: Ra Joon-mo, the main variety PD in The Producers.

examples.trans: Joon-mo, come over here for a second.
Joon-mo is a variety department PD.

meanings.en: how much / how many / how long
meanings.note: Asks about degree, amount, price, or duration

examples.trans: How much will the repair cost be?
How long does it take from here to the station?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 사고잖아, 내가 아는 척하면 너나 나나 괜히 어색해질 수도 있고.
examples.trans: It was a drunken accident—and if I acted like I knew, things could turn needlessly awkward for both of us.
This expression comes from 'grow awkward'.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

examples.trans: Look at me—I blurted mine out over drinks with zero preview, and look how awkward things got with Joon-mo! Previews matter in real life too, not just on television.
The topic of hardship, trouble is this came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.
Health is the most important thing.
There is an important meeting today.

examples.trans: Look at me—I blurted mine out over drinks with zero preview, and look how awkward things got with Joon-mo! Previews matter in real life too, not just on television.
The topic of even in real life came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Interrogative determiner placed directly before a noun.
Indefinite determiner referring to an unspecified person or thing.

examples.trans: What kind of movies do you like?
Some person called.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
